fullCompressions.label: Full Compressions
fullCompressions.why: Below {minCm} cm the heart isn't squeezed hard enough and blood doesn't circulate.

fullRebounds.label: Full Rebounds
fullRebounds.why: Leaning on the chest stops the heart filling: it pumps less blood and less reaches the brain. It's the most common mistake.

averageDepth.label: Average Depth
averageDepth.why: Under {minCm} cm doesn't move enough blood; over {maxCm} cm raises the risk of fractures.

averageBpm.label: Average Rate
averageBpm.why: Below {min} circulation isn't sustained; above {max} the heart has no time to refill. That's about 2 compressions per second.

tips.rateSlow: Compress more often: {min} to {max} per minute, about 2 per second. Below that, blood doesn't reach the brain. Follow the beat of the metronome.
tips.rateFast: Ease the pace back to {min}-{max} per minute. Any faster and the heart can't refill between compressions.
tips.rateUnsteady: Hold an even {min} to {max} per minute. Speeding up and slowing down interrupts blood flow; consistency is what sustains it.
tips.depthShallow: Compress deeper: {minCm} to {maxCm} cm every time. Fall short and the heart doesn't empty. Straight arms, shoulders over your hands, and drop your body weight instead of pushing with your arms.
tips.depthDeep: Ease off a little: don't go past {maxCm} cm. Deeper doesn't pump more blood and raises the risk of rib injury.
tips.depthInconsistent: Several compressions fell short of {minCm} cm. That usually happens near the end as your arms tire: hold the depth through the last one, and in a real emergency swap rescuers every 2 minutes.
tips.recoil: Let the chest come all the way back between compressions. Without lifting your hands, release your weight completely: lean in and the heart won't refill, so the next compression pumps almost nothing.

summary.excellent: Textbook technique across all {total} compressions. In a real emergency, don't stop until help arrives.
summary.good: Strong run. Fix the one point flagged below and the technique is textbook.
summary.fair: Solid base. Work on the points flagged below and you'll improve fast.
summary.keepPracticing: Good first go. Read the points flagged below and try again — technique is learned by repeating it.

instructions.pageSubtitle:
Here's your step-by-step guide to performing
Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation like a pro.
instructions.challengeStarts: The CPR challenge is about to begin...

step1.title: Hands at the heart
step1.description: Place your hands in the center of the chest, one on top of the other, with your fingers interlaced.

step2.title: Lock those elbows
step2.description: Keep your arms straight and lock your elbows to use your upper body weight.

step3.title: Use your body weight
step3.description: Let your body weight do the work, it's not about arm strength!

step1.title: Depth
step1.description: Press at least 5cm and no more than 6cm per compression.

step2.title: Rise
step2.description: Let the chest fully rise after each compression.

step3.title: Rhythm
step3.description: Maintain a rhythm of 100-120 compressions per minute ~ 2/sec.

step4.title: Cycle
step4.description: 30 compressions, then 2 rescue breaths if you are trained.

goals.title: Your goals
goals.rhythm:
Maintain 100-120 compressions per minute or approximately ~ 2 per second.
Follow the beat of the metronome
goals.depth: Achieve 5cm depth for each compression (you will hear a 'click')
goals.recoil: Allow the chest to fully rise after each compression
